visible.presentation_text:
Consult request from the facility's licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

Eastern gray squirrel, approximately 14 weeks, raised from four days of age by a member of the public who kept it for nine weeks before surrendering it. Hand-reared without conspecifics and handled daily.

Animal is fully weaned, eating a varied natural diet, maintaining weight, caching food, and physically normal on examination. No injuries, no disease findings. Coat and dentition normal. Active, climbing, and using enrichment.

Animal was habituated to humans on admission. After four weeks of soft-release conditioning, partial avoidance has been restored: the animal now retreats from direct approach and no longer solicits contact, though it still tolerates human presence at close range. Habituated squirrels released in this region have a documented pattern of returning to human dwellings, entering structures, and generating conflict calls, which typically end in lethal removal by a licensed problem-animal control agent.

Animal is non-releasable on behavioral grounds. Massachusetts does not permit private possession of native wildlife. Educational placement: gray squirrels are not in demand as program animals; two nature centers contacted, neither accepting. No breeding or research use.

Permanent captivity would require an indoor enclosure with vertical space, daily care, and would occupy a caging unit for an expected 6–10 years. Housing cost is modest.
menu_options: Continue holding while placement is sought
Attempt release at a distant site
Transfer the animal to another facility
